# Let me try a completely different approach
# Move player to the right edge where green blocks were initially
# and see if clicking on them works

# First, let me check the current player position and move right
seg = current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] == 'b':
        b = n['boundary']
        cols = [p[1] for p in b]
        player_col = min(cols)
        print(f"Player col: {player_col}")

# Move player all the way to the right
result = action(['RIGHT'] * 40)
print(f"\nAfter moving right:")

seg2 = current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg2['nodes']:
    if n['color'] in ['b', 'Y', 'N', 'P']:
        b = n['boundary']
        rows = [p[0] for p in b]
        cols = [p[1] for p in b]
        print(f"{n['color']}: ({min(rows)},{min(cols)})-({max(rows)},{max(cols)}), {n['pixels']} pixels")

# Now try clicking on green blocks
# Find green block positions
green_blocks = [n for n in seg2['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N']
print(f"\nGreen blocks: {len(green_blocks)}")
for gb in green_blocks:
    b = gb['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    center_r = (min(rows) + max(rows)) // 2
    center_c = (min(cols) + max(cols)) // 2
    print(f"  Green at ({min(rows)},{min(cols)})-({max(rows)},{max(cols)}), center=({center_r},{center_c})")
    
    # Try clicking on this green block
    result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': center_r, 'col': center_c}])
    print(f"  Click ({center_r},{center_c}): gameplay_changed={result.get('gameplay_changed')}")
    
    # Check if green block was removed
    seg3 = current_frame.segmentation
    green_count = sum(1 for n in seg3['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N')
    print(f"  Green blocks remaining: {green_count}")
    if result.get('done') or result.get('level_completed'):
        break
